## Optionally MINT a new phase
If an objective signal calls for work no existing phase covers, you MAY add an entry for a brand-new phase by attaching a "mint" block. Give it a kebab-case phase name, an inline persona prompt, and a TIER (fast|balanced|deep — never a raw model name). Minted phases are always optional and clamped by the kernel; they can never reach ship without audit. Omit "mint" for existing phases. Minted phases default to writes_source:true; set "writes_source":false only for phases that never edit source.
ALSO supply "description" (one line: what the phase produces) and "when_to_use" (the signal that should trigger SELECTing it) — this is the SELECT metadata a later cycle reads to reuse your phase instead of minting a duplicate.

You MAY also propose a dispatch "cli" and abstract "tier" (fast|balanced|deep — never a raw model name) for an EXISTING phase, honoring its allowed_clis/model_tier_envelope above when shown. Omit both to leave the phase's profile-pinned default unchanged.

## Operator model-tier policy (apply when proposing a tier)
- deep: judgment-heavy phases — build, tdd, audit, architecture/design, adversarial review.
- balanced: review/scan/triage-class phases — the safe default for anything not covered below.
- fast: ONLY mechanical phases (doc-sync, changelog-sync, locale-format-check, close-checklist) — NEVER for a phase that writes source, renders a verdict, or scopes work. When in doubt, propose HIGHER.
- Judgment phases usually carry a min=balanced envelope above — don't fight the clamp with a low-tier proposal; propose a CLI only when deviating from the phase's profile default is justified.
